en: Vimānavatthu:
Purisavimāna,
Pāyāsivagga
10. (Uttara) The Mansion of Pāyāsi:
“That Sudhamma assembly hall of the king of the gods, where the entire host of deities gathers together;”
Just like that, this celestial mansion of yours stands illuminating the sky.
You have attained the power of a deva, O one of great majesty.
"What merit did you perform while being a human being?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing majesty,
and why does your complexion illuminate all directions?"
Thus the young deva was delighted...
[as before] ...the fruit of which deed this is.
“Among humans, having become human,
I was a young brahmin in the service of King Pāyāsi;
having acquired wealth, I practiced sharing it.
And those who were virtuous were dear to me;
with a confident heart, I gave abundant gifts of food and drink with due respect.
"Because of that, my complexion is such as this...
and my complexion shines forth in all directions."
The *Pāyāsi-vimāna* is the tenth.
The sixth chapter, the *Pāyāsi-vagga*.
Its summary verse (*uddāna*) is as follows:
Two householders who give fruit,
two who give lodging, and one who gives alms;
and a barley-guardian, and two more.
"Kuṇḍalino pāyāsī" is proclaimed as the second chapter of men.
